sentences.text: Crichtonpelta was a herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in China during the Late Cretaceous.
A unique derived trait of Crichtonpelta is that the apex of its cheek horn points upwards.
The armor on the upper snout of Crichtonpelta formed an amorphous mass rather than distinct tiles.
The genus name honors author Michael Crichton and the Greek word for a small shield.
The holotype specimen was somewhat larger than the related species Crichtonsaurus, which measured about 3 to 4 meters in length.
The species was originally described in 2007 by Lü Junchang, Ji Qiang, Gao Yubo, and Li Zhixin under the name Crichtonsaurus benxiensis.
The holotype specimen BXGMV0012 is a skull found near Beipiao in the Sunjiawan Formation, dating to approximately 99–95 million years ago.
The genus was validly established in 2015 by Victoria Arbour and Philip John Currie.
Victoria Arbour created the separate genus Crichtonpelta in 2014 because she considered the original genus Crichtonsaurus to be a nomen dubium.
Crichtonpelta is classified within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae of the family Ankylosauridae.
The fossil record for Crichtonpelta spans from the Albian to the Turonian stages, between 106.3 and 89.8 million years ago.
If its basal position within Ankylosaurinae is correct, Crichtonpelta would be the oldest known ankylosaurine.
There is a possibility that fossil material previously referred to Crichtonsaurus bohlini actually belongs to Crichtonpelta.
It is currently uncertain whether Crichtonpelta possessed a tail club.
